newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down 13 cts but well above days low.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down 13 cts but well above days low.

text.p: IPE Brent futures for February ended down 13 cents a barrel on Friday but well above the days lows following a late recovery.
The last trade on February at $24.09 a barrel leaves Brent above the psycologically important $24.00 level and compares to a low of $23.80 hit during the afternoon.
Dealers said the move lower was an attempt to fill a chart gap between $23.82 and $24.04 a barrel left after the market jumped higher on Thursday. Fridays trade range was from $23.80 to $24.15.
"The weakness did look pretty technical. The physical market held pretty steady," said a Brent cargo trader.

Weakness earlier in the day was due to falling gas oil prices and bearish stock data from the United States. But despite those pressures the physical market for Brent crude and other North Sea grades was little changed from Thursday.
Inter-month spreads on IPE Brent weakened sharply flattening the backwardation and reflecting a similar move on gas oil futures which closed about three hours earlier.
Some dealers expected the market to recover quickly next week and resume an assault on the $25.06 a barrel six year high which was set about three months ago.
"The bias is still upwards as long as the cold weather persists," said a broker.
More than 150 people have died across Europe as the coldest weather in up to 30 years has trapped travellers, frozen rivers and sent energy demand soaring.

Earlier gas oil futures ended $4.25 a tonne lower for January at $227.75 but above the days low of $226.75 set around midday. Feb and March ended $3.50 and $2.25 lower respectively as intermonth spreads crumbled after the bearish U.S. stock data.
